title: Predict the output: string concatenation with null
shortTitle: Predict the output: string concatenation with null
keyPoints: "Hello" + null = "Hellonull" – the + operator converts null to the String "null"
null.concat("Hello") throws NullPointerException – concat() is a method call on null
System.out.println(null) prints "null" – println calls String.valueOf(null) which returns "null"
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level

s1_definition.oneliner: "Hello" + null = "Hellonull". The + operator converts null to the String "null". But null.concat() throws NPE because you are calling a method on null.
s1_definition.profdef:
null in string context:

- **+ operator:** Calls String.valueOf(null) which returns "null" (the String). No exception.
- **concat() method:** Calling any method on null throws NullPointerException.
- **println(null):** Calls String.valueOf(null) → prints "null".
s1_definition.analogy: The + operator is like a polite clerk who writes "null" on the form when a field is empty. The concat() method is like asking an absent clerk (null) to do work – nobody is there, so it crashes.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The + operator converts null to the String "null" and concatenates safely. But calling concat() or any method on a null reference throws NullPointerException.

One sentence to remember: + converts null to "null" (safe), concat() on null throws NPE (crash).
